issue_context.title: promtool test with `/dev/stdin` fails for multiple test cases
issue_context.body:
### What did you do?

I use `promtool` test with the following rules and tests:

## rules
```yaml
# prometheus-rules.yml
apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: PrometheusRule
spec:
  groups:
    - name: myalerts
      rules:
        - alert: ErrorInLog
          expr: changes(log_messages_total{log_level="ERROR"}[1m]) > 0
          annotations:
            summary: 'New error(s) appeared in the log of container {{ $labels.container }}'
        - alert: NoNewMessages
          expr: sum(increase(messages_sent_total[3m])) == 0
          annotations:
            summary: 'My component did not send any messages for 3 minutes'
```

## tests
```yaml
# test-alerts.yml
rule_files:
  - /dev/stdin

tests:
  - name: 'Should trigger if no messages were sent for more than 3 minutes'
    interval: 1m
    input_series:
      - series: 'messages_sent_total'
        values: '0 0 0 0'
    alert_rule_test:
      - eval_time: 4m
        alertname: NoNewMessages
        exp_alerts:
          - exp_annotations:
              summary: 'My component did not send any messages for 3 minutes'
  - name: 'should trigger in case an error is detected'
    interval: 1m
    input_series:
      - series: 'log_messages_total{container="mycontainer", log_level="ERROR"}'
        values: '0 1 2'
    alert_rule_test:
      - eval_time: 2m
        alertname: ErrorInLog
        exp_alerts:
          - exp_labels:
              log_level: "ERROR"
              container: "mycontainer"
            exp_annotations:
              summary: 'New error(s) appeared in the log of container mycontainer'
```

It seems that there is a bug with the way promtool reads from `/dev/stdin` compared to executing the tests with a static file.

### What did you expect to see?

The same tests with a static input file (`alerts.yaml`) pass:

```bash
 yq .spec prometheus-rules.yml > alerts.yaml && promtool test  rules test-alerts.yml && rm alerts.yaml
Unit Testing:  test-alerts.yml
  SUCCESS
```

### What did you see instead? Under which circumstances?

The tests fail for `/dev/stdin`:
```bash
 yq .spec prometheus-rules.yml | promtool test  rules test-alerts.yml
Unit Testing:  test-alerts.yml
  FAILED:
    name: should trigger in case an error is detected,
    alertname: ErrorInLog, time: 2m, 
        exp:[
            0:
              Labels:{alertname="ErrorInLog", container="mycontainer", log_level="ERROR"}
              Annotations:{summary="New error(s) appeared in the log of container mycontainer"}
            ], 
        got:[]
```

### System information

macOS 14.4

### Prometheus version

```text
promtool, version 2.50.1 (branch: non-git, revision: non-git)
  build user:       brew@Sonoma-arm64.local
  build date:       20240226-11:31:35
  go version:       go1.22.0
  platform:         darwin/arm64
  tags:             netgo,builtinassets,stringlabels
```


### Prometheus configuration file

_No response_

### Alertmanager version

_No response_

### Alertmanager configuration file

_No response_

### Logs

_No response_
comments: The key here is multiple, each test reads from /dev/stdin. I think it would be useful to support use cases like your `yq` one by buffering to a temp file so it works.

Also you don't see a read error because further reads from `/dev/stdin` are reading from the open FD, which has reached the end, so each read just gets an EOF. Prometheus in general accepts empty rule files, but it's possible to specially handle this in promtool tests so stdin/pipes get errors on an empty read, I've put something in the PR to deal with that too.

review_comments: I don't know if we can/want to support heredoc as well.

This should work, not entirely sure what the use case would be, but a heredoc becomes a pipe:

```
$ readlink -f /dev/stdin <<EOF
> test
> EOF
/proc/52258/fd/pipe:[232761]
```

One may want to script it like :
```
promtool test rules alerts-test.yaml <<EOF
groups:
- name: myalerts
  rules:
  - alert: NoNewMessages
    expr: sum(increase(messages_sent_total[3m])) == 0
    annotations:
      summary: 'My component did not send any messages for 3 minutes'
EOF
```
question: why those from `io/fs` instead of the ones from `os`, any difference?
The os ones import from io/fs now. I don't really think it makes any difference which way around it is.
